Settings of the posterior computation

Source: R/posterior.R
posterior_control.Rd

Chooses the engine that integrates over the between-site standard deviation and sets its tolerances.

Usage

posterior_control(
  engine = c("nodes", "adaptive"),
  rel_tol = 1e-10,
  abs_tol = 1e-12,
  chunk_sites = 2000
)

Arguments

engine

The engine: "nodes" (the default) builds one quadrature rule and reuses it for every summary of a fit; "adaptive" computes each posterior mean, probability and quantile with stats::integrate(), as Lee (2026, Appendix D.3) describes.

rel_tol, abs_tol

Relative and absolute tolerances of stats::integrate() for the adaptive engine, positive numbers. The absolute tolerance applies to integrands scaled to the size of the posterior and of the integrated quantity, so it does not depend on the units of the estimates.

chunk_sites

Number of sites computed at a time for the site summaries, a positive integer. Smaller values use less memory.

Value

A list of class posterior_control with the components

  • engine: "nodes" or "adaptive".

  • rel_tol, abs_tol: the tolerances of the adaptive engine.

  • chunk_sites: the number of sites computed at a time.

Details

Both engines integrate the same posterior, and their summaries agree to many more digits than are printed. The node rule is the faster: one rule of Gauss-Legendre panels serves every summary of a fit, while the adaptive engine integrates each summary, and each site, separately. The adaptive engine takes the posterior standard deviations, and the intervals of the site effects and of the coefficients, from a node rule. vignette("implementation") describes the rule, its checks and the comparison of the engines. With a prior whose tail is very heavy, such as a half-t prior with far fewer than one degree of freedom, a moment can exist and still have a tail too slow for the rule to bound. Both engines then stop with an error that names the moment. A moment that does not exist is NA instead. vignette("implementation") gives the limits.

See also

reliability_posterior(), whose argument control takes these settings, and check_numerics() for the checks of a fit.

Examples

posterior_control()
#> Posterior computation: nodes engine
posterior_control(engine = "adaptive")
#> Posterior computation: adaptive engine, rel_tol 1e-10, abs_tol 1e-12
